brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: One keyhole hanger on the back face (slot 3) of each cell: accessory:0#0,0#3, accessory:1#0,0#3 and accessory:2#0,0#3. The faces are stacked, so all three sit flat against the wall.
Nine hook plates (18 hooks) on slots 0, 1 and 5 at levels 0–2, for example accessory:0#0,0#0 and accessory:2#0,0#5.
The final check found no rule errors and the mesh-collision check came back clear. The only note was informational: some open faces could take caps.

finish.summary:
I built a wall-hung tool rack: three full cells stacked in one column at (0,0), levels 0–2, joined by two snaps. A keyhole hanger sits on the back face (slot 3) of each cell. Nine hook plates, with two hooks each (18 hooks), cover the front and the two front-angled faces (slots 0, 1 and 5) on every level. The final check found no rule errors and the mesh-collision check came back clear. The only note was informational: some open faces could take caps.

**Why it's a single column:** in a sideways row of hex cells, the outward faces don't line up in one flat plane, so they couldn't all sit flush against a wall. In a vertical column, the three back faces stack into one flat plane, so all three keyhole hangers bear on the same wall.

This confirms the parts fit together. It doesn't tell you how much weight the rack can hold.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
